This also sends the view state on every call.
Polling wastes requests and doesn't react to typing.
questions.source: Visualforce Developer Guide: JavaScript Remoting for Apex Controllers

questions.q: A custom JavaScript date-picker on a Visualforce page must, when a date is picked, set a controller property, run a `recalculate()` action that updates other controller properties, and redraw only the totals section. Which approach fits best?
options: A `@RemoteAction` method called with `Visualforce.remoting.Manager.invokeAction` that recalculates and returns the totals
`apex:actionPoller` with `interval="1"`
An `apex:commandLink` with no `rerender` attribute
`apex:actionFunction` with `action="{!recalculate}"`, `rerender="totals"` and an `apex:param`, called from the picker's JS
questions.explain: When custom JS must run a controller action and redraw part of the page, use `actionFunction`. It works inside the page's state, passes values with `apex:param`, and redraws with `rerender`.
wrong: Remote actions are static and stateless; they can't update the page's controller or rerender parts.
Polling is wasteful and doesn't respond to the picker.
Without `rerender` the whole page refreshes, and custom JS can't cleanly pass it a value.
questions.source: Visualforce Developer Guide: apex:actionFunction

questions.q: A Visualforce page shows a comment field with `<apex:outputText value="{!comment}" escape="false"/>`. A security review flags it. What is the risk?
options: SOQL injection
Cross-site scripting (XSS): user-entered HTML or script is rendered unescaped
View state tampering
Cross-site request forgery, because `escape="false"` also removes the page's anti-CSRF token
questions.explain: Visualforce escapes output by default so typed HTML shows as text. `escape="false"` turns that off. Now stored script can run in other users' browsers: that's **XSS**.
wrong: No query is built from this value, so there's no SOQL injection.
View state is encrypted; this issue is about output encoding.
`escape` only affects output encoding, not CSRF protection.
questions.source: Secure Coding Guide: Cross-Site Scripting / Visualforce Developer Guide

questions.q: A Visualforce page contains the script below. How should the developer prevent script injection through the URL parameter?
questions.code:
<script>
  var acct = '{!$CurrentPage.parameters.acct}';
</script>
options: Use `'{!HTMLENCODE($CurrentPage.parameters.acct)}'`
Use `'{!URLENCODE($CurrentPage.parameters.acct)}'`
Use `'{!JSENCODE($CurrentPage.parameters.acct)}'`
Move the script into a static resource without changing the merge field
questions.explain: Match the encoding to the spot where the value lands. Inside a JavaScript string, use `JSENCODE`. It escapes quotes and backslashes, so the value can't break out of the string.
wrong: HTML encoding doesn't protect a JavaScript string.
URL encoding is for URLs, not JS strings.
Merge fields don't work in static resources, and moving the script doesn't fix encoding.
questions.source: Visualforce Developer Guide: Security Tips for Apex and Visualforce (JSENCODE)

questions.q: An LWC must use a third-party charting library and call `fetch()` on a partner's REST endpoint directly from the browser. Both currently fail in Lightning Experience. Which two actions are needed? (Choose 2)
options: Add a `<script src="https://cdn...">` tag to the template
Upload the library as a static resource and load it with `loadScript` from `lightning/platformResourceLoader`
Turn off Lightning Web Security in Session Settings
Add a Remote Site Setting for the partner endpoint
Add the partner domain as a Trusted URL (CSP) with `connect-src` allowed
questions.explain: CSP blocks scripts from outside Salesforce and browser calls to unknown domains. Fix the library with a static resource plus `loadScript`. Fix the `fetch()` by adding the domain as a Trusted URL.
wrong: LWC templates can't hold script tags, and CSP blocks CDN scripts.
LWS isn't what blocks these, and turning off security is never a valid fix.
Remote Site Settings allow server-side Apex callouts, not browser requests.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Content Security Policy / Use Third-Party JavaScript Libraries

questions.q: An `@AuraEnabled(cacheable=true)` method returns Contacts, including `SSN__c`, to an LWC data table. The class is declared `with sharing`, yet users without FLS on `SSN__c` can still see the values. Which two changes enforce field-level security? (Choose 2)
options: Add `WITH USER_MODE` to the SOQL query
Change the class to `inherited sharing`
Rely on Lightning Web Security to hide the field
Remove `cacheable=true`
Pass the query results through `Security.stripInaccessible(AccessType.READABLE, records)`
questions.explain: Sharing keywords decide which records you see, not which fields. To enforce FLS, add `WITH USER_MODE` to the query. Or pass the results through `Security.stripInaccessible`, which removes unreadable fields.
wrong: `inherited sharing` is still about record sharing, not FLS.
LWS isolates JavaScript namespaces; it doesn't apply data permissions.
Caching has no effect on field-level security.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Enforce User Mode / Security.stripInaccessible

questions.q: The finance team at a wholesale distributor wants a "Generate Invoice" button on Opportunity. It must produce a printable invoice that matches their paper letterhead and save the file to the record, with no third-party JavaScript library. Most users work in Lightning Experience; a few still use the desktop Outlook integration. Which solution should the developer build?
options: An LWC headless quick action that calls `window.print()` and saves the printed output with `lightning-file-upload` on the Opportunity record
A Visualforce page with `renderAs="pdf"`, and Apex that calls `getContentAsPDF()` and saves the Blob as a `ContentVersion` on the record
An Aura component that sets `renderAs="pdf"` on its `aura:component` tag and is added as a quick action
An LWC that sets `renderMode="pdf"` in its `js-meta.xml` and is placed on the Opportunity record page
questions.explain: Only Visualforce can render a page as a PDF, with `renderAs="pdf"`. Apex then gets that PDF as a Blob with `PageReference.getContentAsPDF()`. It saves it as a `ContentVersion` on the record.
wrong: `window.print()` opens the print dialog; it creates no file, and file upload needs the user to pick one.
`renderAs` belongs to `apex:page`; Aura has no PDF rendering option.
`js-meta.xml` has no `renderMode="pdf"`; LWC can't render itself as a PDF.
questions.source: Visualforce Developer Guide: Render a Visualforce Page as a PDF File

questions.q: A service team built a new case intake LWC and wants it to replace the standard New button on Case in Lightning Experience. The component is deployed with the configuration below, but when the admin opens Buttons, Links, and Actions > New > Lightning Experience Override, the component is not in the list. What should the developer do?
questions.code:
<LightningComponentBundle xmlns="http://soap.sforce.com/2006/04/metadata">
  <apiVersion>62.0</apiVersion>
  <isExposed>true</isExposed>
  <targets>
    <target>lightning__RecordPage</target>
    <target>lightning__RecordAction</target>
  </targets>
</LightningComponentBundle>
options: Add `lightning__UrlAddressable` to targets so the override can open the component by URL
Add a `targetConfig` for `lightning__RecordAction` with `actionType="Override"` and `<object>Case</object>`, then redeploy
Wrap the LWC in an Aura component that implements `lightning:actionOverride`, and pick that as the override
Set `isExposed` to true on the Case object's page layout and redeploy
questions.explain: Only Aura components that implement `lightning:actionOverride` appear in the list for standard button overrides. So wrap the LWC in a thin Aura component with that interface, and pick the wrapper.
wrong: `lightning__UrlAddressable` makes it reachable by URL, not available as an override.
`actionType` only accepts `ScreenAction` or `Action`; there is no Override type.
`isExposed` lives in `js-meta.xml`, not on page layouts, and it's already true.
questions.source: Lightning Aura Components Developer Guide: Creating an Aura Component for Use as an Action Override

questions.q: A team is replacing an Aura `force:navigateToComponent` call. The target LWC, `c-shipment-detail`, has the `lightning__UrlAddressable` target, and it reads the shipment Id from the URL state. Clicking the button opens the component, but it always shows "No shipment selected". What is the cause?
options: State keys must have a namespace prefix, so the caller must pass `c__shipmentId` instead of `shipmentId`
`componentName` must be written in kebab case, such as `c-shipment-detail`
`standard__component` pages cannot receive state, so the Id must be stored in `sessionStorage`
`CurrentPageReference` only works on record pages, so the target must also have `lightning__RecordPage`
questions.explain: Page reference state keys need a namespace prefix, like `c__shipmentId`, and string values. The caller sent plain `shipmentId`, so the target never finds `c__shipmentId`.
wrong: `componentName` uses the `namespace__name` format (`c__shipmentDetail`), which the caller already uses.
`standard__component` does pass state, as URL query parameters.
`CurrentPageReference` works on any Lightning page, not just record pages.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: lightning__UrlAddressable Target

questions.q: An org is moving to Lightning Experience, but a regional team will stay on Salesforce Classic for another year. The architect asks which of these requirements must still be built with Visualforce instead of an LWC or Aura component. Which two? (Choose 2)
options: A page that renders a quote as a PDF using the platform's rendering service
An item in a Lightning console app's utility bar that shows open tasks
A quick action on Account that runs custom code without opening a modal
A replacement for the standard Edit button that must work for the Salesforce Classic users
A custom screen component that collects input inside a screen flow
questions.explain: Two jobs still need Visualforce. PDF rendering (`renderAs="pdf"`) exists only there. And Aura overrides don't work in Salesforce Classic, so Classic users need a Visualforce override.
wrong: An LWC can be a utility item with the `lightning__UtilityBar` target.
An LWC can be a headless quick action with `lightning__RecordAction` and `actionType="Action"`.
An LWC can be a flow screen component with the `lightning__FlowScreen` target.
questions.source: Lightning Aura Components Developer Guide: Standard Actions and Overrides Basics

questions.q: A logistics company has a Node.js customer portal hosted outside Salesforce. Portal users already sign in to Salesforce through OAuth. The company wants to reuse an existing custom LWC that tracks deliveries on one of the portal pages, without rewriting it. What should the developer use?
options: Add the portal domain as a CSP Trusted Site so the portal can load the component from its Lightning Experience URL
`apex:includeLightning` and `$Lightning.createComponent()` in the portal's own HTML page
An Experience Cloud LWR site with a custom domain that matches the portal
Lightning Out, which embeds Lightning web components in external, non-Salesforce web apps
questions.explain: To show an LWC inside a site that isn't on Salesforce, use **Lightning Out** (Lightning Out 2.0, or the older beta). The outside app handles sign-in, which the portal already does through OAuth.
wrong: CSP Trusted Sites let Salesforce pages reach other domains, not outside sites host Salesforce components.
`apex:includeLightning` is a Visualforce tag; it can't run in a Node.js page.
An Experience Cloud site is a separate Salesforce site; it doesn't embed into the Node.js portal.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Use Components Outside Salesforce with Lightning Out 2.0

questions.q: In a Lightning console app, an LWC in the utility bar publishes the selected customer on a message channel. A second LWC sits on the Account record page, which agents usually keep open in several workspace tabs. Only the subscriber in the focused tab updates, but every open tab must update. What should the developer change?
options: Import `APPLICATION_SCOPE` and pass `{ scope: APPLICATION_SCOPE }` as the fourth argument to `subscribe()`
Move the `subscribe()` call from `connectedCallback()` to `renderedCallback()`
Publish the message with `{ scope: APPLICATION_SCOPE }` from the utility bar component instead
Replace the message channel with a `CustomEvent` that has `bubbles: true` and `composed: true`
questions.explain: By default, an LMS subscriber only hears messages while it's in the active area, like the focused tab. Subscribe with `{ scope: APPLICATION_SCOPE }` so components in background tabs hear them too.
wrong: `renderedCallback` runs after every render and would pile up subscriptions; scope is the real problem.
The subscriber sets the scope in `subscribe()`, not the publisher.
DOM events can't travel from the utility bar to a separate tab; they share no DOM tree.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Define the Scope of the Message Service

questions.q: A field sales team wants a "Nearby Visits" component. On Lightning app pages it must appear only on phones. On Account record pages it must appear on both desktop and phone. Which `js-meta.xml` configuration meets this?
questions.code:

<targetConfigs>
  <targetConfig targets="...">
    <supportedFormFactors>
      <supportedFormFactor type="..."/>
    </supportedFormFactors>
  </targetConfig>
</targetConfigs>
options: One `targetConfig` for `"lightning__AppPage,lightning__RecordPage"` with `supportedFormFactor` `type="Small"` only
A `targetConfig` for `lightning__AppPage` with `type="Small"`, and a `targetConfig` for `lightning__RecordPage` with `type="Large"` and `type="Small"`
A `targetConfig` for `lightning__AppPage` with `type="Phone"`, and a `targetConfig` for `lightning__RecordPage` with `type="Desktop"` and `type="Phone"`
A `supportedFormFactors` block directly under `<targets>`, listing `type="Small"` for app pages and `type="Medium"` for record pages
questions.explain: Device rules go inside each `targetConfig`, so every page type can have its own devices. App pages get `Small` only. Record pages get `Large` and `Small`.
wrong: One shared `targetConfig` would limit record pages to phones too, so desktop users lose it.
`Phone` and `Desktop` aren't valid types; the values are `Small` and `Large`.
`supportedFormFactors` can't sit directly under targets, and `Medium` isn't valid for pages.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Configure Your Component for Different Form Factors

questions.q: A developer wants a compact card layout for phone users of the Salesforce mobile app and the full table on desktop. Testers on phones always see the full table. What is the bug?
options: `formFactor` must be read in `connectedCallback()`, because the module value is not ready when the getter runs
The value for a phone is `'PHONE'`, the same as `$Browser.formFactor` in Aura
The value for a phone is `'Small'`, so the getter should compare `FORM_FACTOR` to `'Small'`
Getters are not reactive, so `isPhone` must be a field decorated with `@track`
questions.explain: The LWC form factor module uses size words, not device words. `@salesforce/client/formFactor` returns `Large` (desktop), `Medium` (tablet) or `Small` (phone). So comparing to `'Phone'` is never true.
wrong: The imported value is ready as soon as the module loads, so a getter can read it anytime.
`PHONE` comes from Aura's `$Browser`, not from the LWC `formFactor` module.
The getter returns a constant, so reactivity isn't the issue, and `@track` wouldn't fix the comparison.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Access Client Form Factor

questions.q: On a phone, the two panels below appear squeezed side by side instead of stacked. On desktops they should sit side by side at half width each. Which two changes fix the layout? (Choose 2)
questions.code:
<lightning-layout>
  <lightning-layout-item medium-device-size="6" padding="around-small">
    <c-account-summary></c-account-summary>
  </lightning-layout-item>
  <lightning-layout-item medium-device-size="6" padding="around-small">
    <c-open-cases></c-open-cases>
  </lightning-layout-item>
</lightning-layout>
options: Replace `medium-device-size="6"` with `small-device-size="12"` only
Add `size="12"` to each `lightning-layout-item`
Add `flexibility="auto"` to `lightning-layout`
Wrap each item in a div with class `slds-hide_medium`
Add `multiple-rows="true"` to `lightning-layout` so items can wrap onto new rows
questions.explain: Device-size attributes only work when `size` is also set. `size="12"` makes each item full width on phones, and `medium-device-size="6"` takes over from tablets up. `multiple-rows="true"` lets full-width items wrap onto new rows.
wrong: `small-device-size` still needs `size` set, and it would make items full width on bigger screens too.
`flexibility` belongs on `lightning-layout-item`, and auto sizing doesn't force items to stack.
`slds-hide_medium` hides content from medium screens up, so desktops would lose the panels.
questions.source: Lightning Component Reference: lightning-layout-item

questions.q: An Aura component on a record page should show a short summary on phones and a detailed view on desktop. On phones it always shows the detailed view. Which two changes would make the phone check work? (Choose 2)

Compare `$Browser.formFactor` to `'small'` in lowercase
Compare `$Browser.formFactor` to `'PHONE'`
Use `{!$Browser.isPhone}` as the condition
Add a `design:supportedFormFactor` of type `Small` to the component's `.design` file
questions.explain: Aura's `$Browser` uses its own capital-letter words. `$Browser.formFactor` returns values like `DESKTOP` and `PHONE`, and `$Browser.isPhone` is true on phones. `Small` and `Large` belong to LWC and page settings.
wrong: `@salesforce` scoped modules are for LWC, not Aura controllers.
The value is `PHONE`, so lowercasing `'Small'` doesn't help.
The `.design` file controls where App Builder offers the component, not which markup it shows.
questions.source: Lightning Aura Components Developer Guide: $Browser

questions.q: A Visualforce page styled with `apex:slds` shows a set of product tiles. Product owners want one tile per row on phones, two per row on tablets and three per row on desktops. Each tile is a div inside a parent div. Which classes should the developer use?

...
...
...
options: Parent: `slds-grid`; tile: `slds-size_1-of-3 slds-medium-size_1-of-2 slds-small-size_1-of-1`

questions.q: An Aura wrapper contains an LWC that lets agents pick a warranty plan. The LWC dispatches the event below. Which line in the Aura controller correctly reads the selected plan Id?
options: `component.get('v.planId')`
`event.getSource().get('v.selectedPlanId')`
`event.target.value`
`event.getParam('planId')`
questions.explain: When Aura handles a DOM event from an LWC, each key in the event's `detail` becomes a parameter. Read it with `event.getParam('planId')`.
wrong: This reads the wrapper's own attribute, which isn't set yet.
`selectedPlanId` is a private LWC field, not an Aura attribute, so it can't be read this way.

questions.q: An Aura app page component contains an LWC with an `@api` method called `loadDefaults()`. The Aura component calls it from its init handler, but the browser console shows an error and the defaults never load. What is the cause?
questions.code:
<!-- quoteShell.cmp -->
<aura:component implements="flexipage:availableForAllPageTypes">
  <aura:handler name="init" value="{!this}" action="{!c.doInit}"/>
  <c:quoteLines aura:id="lines"/>
</aura:component>

// quoteShellController.js
doInit: function (component) {
  component.find('lines').loadDefaults();
}
options: Aura cannot call LWC methods. The LWC must listen for an Aura application event instead
The LWC is not created until the Aura component renders, so its method cannot be called during init
`aura:id` does not work on LWCs. The method must be found with `document.querySelector('c-quote-lines')`
The method name must be in kebab case, such as `component.find('lines')['load-defaults']()`
questions.explain: An LWC inside Aura doesn't exist until the Aura component renders. Aura can call its `@api` method with `component.find()`, but not during init. So the call fails.
wrong: Aura can call an LWC's public method with `component.find('auraId').methodName()`.
`aura:id` works on LWCs in Aura markup, and document queries break encapsulation.
JavaScript methods keep their camelCase name; kebab case is only for HTML attributes.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Compose Aura Components from Lightning Web Components

questions.q: A Reset button in an Aura wrapper should clear the filters in a child LWC. Clicking it throws "`component.find(...).clearFilters` is not a function". What should the developer change?
options: Decorate `clearFilters()` with `@api` so the parent can call it
Rename the method to `setClearFilters()` so Aura treats it as a setter
Fire an Aura component event from the wrapper and handle it in the LWC with `aura:handler`
Change `objectName` to a method so Aura sees the component as public
questions.explain: A parent can only call a child's method if the method is public. Decorate `clearFilters()` with `@api`. That's true whether the parent is Aura or LWC.
wrong: Aura doesn't treat methods starting with `set` as public.
An LWC can't use `aura:handler` or handle Aura component events.
One public property doesn't make other methods public; each method needs `@api`.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Compose Aura Components from Lightning Web Components

questions.q: An LWC (`c-region-picker`) sits inside Aura component A, which is inside Aura component B. The picker dispatches a `regionchange` event. Component B must react, but a handler that B puts on its `<c:componentA>` tag never runs. Which two approaches work? (Choose 2)
options: Handle `onregionchange` on the `<c:regionPicker>` tag in component A, then fire an Aura component event that B handles
Dispatch the event with `bubbles: true` and `composed: true` so B's `onregionchange` handler on `<c:componentA>` catches it
Publish the region on a Lightning message channel from the LWC and subscribe in B with `lightning:messageChannel`
Add `<aura:handler name="regionchange" action="{!c.handle}"/>` to component B
Register the event in the LWC with `<aura:registerEvent name="regionchange" type="c:regionEvt"/>`
questions.explain: An `onxxx` handler for an LWC event can only sit in the first Aura component the event reaches, here A. A can pass the news on with an Aura event. Or skip nesting entirely with Lightning Message Service, which links LWC and Aura directly.
wrong: The docs say only the first Aura component the event bubbles to can handle it, so B still can't.
A named `aura:handler` handles Aura component events, not DOM events from an LWC.
`aura:registerEvent` is Aura markup; LWCs can't fire Aura events.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Send Events to an Enclosing Aura Component

questions.q: A Visualforce page on an Account Lightning record page subscribes to a message channel that an LWC publishes on. The page updates correctly in Lightning Experience on desktop, but sales reps say it never updates in the Salesforce mobile app. What is the most likely reason?

<apex:page>
  <script>
    var CHANNEL = "{!$MessageChannel.Account_Selected__c}";
    var sub;
    function startListening() {
      if (!sub) {
        sub = sforce.one.subscribe(CHANNEL, onAccount, { scope: "APPLICATION" });
      }
    }
    function onAccount(msg) { /* update the page */ }
    startListening();
  </script>
</apex:page>
options: The channel must be referenced as `$MessageChannel.Account_Selected` instead of with the `__c` suffix on mobile
The `scope` option must be removed, because `APPLICATION` scope is not allowed on mobile
The LWC must publish with `sforce.one.publish()` so that the Visualforce page can receive it
Lightning Message Service supports Aura and LWC in the mobile app, but not Visualforce (`sforce.one`)
questions.explain: In the Salesforce mobile app, Lightning Message Service works for Aura and LWC only. Visualforce pages there can't send or receive messages. So the code is fine; the platform is the limit.
wrong: The channel API name always keeps the `__c` suffix, on every device.
Dropping the scope won't help, because LMS doesn't support Visualforce in the mobile app.
An LWC publishes with `publish()` from `lightning/messageService`; `sforce.one` is the Visualforce API.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Lightning Message Service Limitations

questions.q: An Aura component must publish the selected order on the `Order_Selected__c` message channel when a button is clicked. Clicking the button throws "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'publish')". What is the fix?

}

Call `$A.get('e.c:Order_Selected__c').fire()` instead of `publish()`
Add `aura:id="orderChannel"` to the `lightning:messageChannel` tag
Set `scope="APPLICATION"` on `lightning:messageChannel`
questions.explain: Aura finds its `lightning:messageChannel` by `aura:id`, then calls `publish()` on it. With no `aura:id`, `cmp.find()` returns `undefined`. Then `.publish` throws.
wrong: `@salesforce` module imports are for LWC; Aura uses the `lightning:messageChannel` tag.
A message channel isn't an Aura application event, so `$A.get()` can't fire it.
`scope` controls which subscribers hear messages; it doesn't fix the missing reference.
questions.source: Lightning Aura Components Developer Guide: Publish on a Message Channel

questions.q: A developer uploaded `chart.js` as a zip static resource named `chartjs_v4`. Inside the zip the file is at `dist/chart.umd.js`. The LWC below shows the error toast on every page load, and the network tab shows a 404 for the script. What is the fix?

Import the file directly with `import CHARTJS from '@salesforce/resourceUrl/chartjs_v4/dist/chart.umd.js'`
Move `loadScript()` into `connectedCallback()`, because `renderedCallback()` runs too late for libraries
Upload the file again as a separate static resource, because `loadScript` cannot read files inside a zip
questions.explain: The imported URL points at the zip itself. Add the path inside it with string joining, and start that path with a slash. Without the slash the URL is wrong and returns 404.
wrong: The import names only the static resource; the inside path is added at runtime.
`renderedCallback` plus a guard flag is the documented pattern, and it doesn't cause a 404.
`loadScript` can read a file from a zip when the path is built correctly.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Access Static Resources

questions.q: A team is planning how to package front-end assets (a 3 MB mapping library, icons and a stylesheet) as static resources for LWC, Aura and Visualforce pages, some of which are used on a public Experience Cloud site. Which two statements are true? (Choose 2)
options: An LWC can load the library by adding `<script src={libUrl}></script>` to its template once the URL is imported
A single static resource can be up to 5 MB, and an org can hold up to 250 MB of static resources
In a Salesforce DX project, assets can be grouped into subfolders of the `staticresources` folder, one per library
With Cache Control set to `Public`, the cached resource can be reached by all internet traffic, including unauthenticated users
A static resource name such as `map-lib-v2` is valid as long as it is unique in the org
questions.explain: The documented limits are **5 MB** per static resource and **250 MB** per org. With Cache Control set to Public, the cached file is shared and reachable by anyone, even signed-out visitors. That matters on public sites.
wrong: LWC templates can't hold script tags; libraries load with `loadScript`.
You can't make subfolders in `staticresources`; use a zip to keep folders.
Names allow only letters, numbers and underscores, so hyphens aren't allowed.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Access Static Resources

questions.q: A field service Visualforce page needs a signature pad library. The developer uploaded a zip static resource named `SignaturePad` that contains `js/signature_pad.min.js`. Which markup loads the script correctly?
options: `<apex:includeScript value="{!$Resource.SignaturePad.js.signature_pad}"/>`
`<ltng:require scripts="{!$Resource.SignaturePad + '/js/signature_pad.min.js'}"/>`
`<apex:includeScript value="{!$Resource['SignaturePad/js/signature_pad.min.js']}"/>`
`<apex:includeScript value="{!URLFOR($Resource.SignaturePad, 'js/signature_pad.min.js')}"/>`
questions.explain: In Visualforce, a file inside a zip static resource needs `URLFOR()`. Pass the resource and the path inside the zip. Plain `$Resource.name` is only for stand-alone files.
wrong: Merge fields can't walk into a zip with dot notation.
`ltng:require` is an Aura tag, not used in Visualforce pages.
The `$Resource` key is the resource name only; the inside path isn't part of it.
questions.source: Visualforce Developer Guide: Referencing a Static Resource in Visualforce Markup

questions.q: An Aura component draws a heat map with two libraries from the `mapLibs` zip: `leaflet.js`, and `heat.js`, which depends on leaflet. Users see "L is not defined" in the console and the map never draws. Which two changes fix it? (Choose 2)
questions.code: // controller doInit: function (component) { var map = L.map(component.find('map').getElement()); }
options: Put each library in its own `ltng:require` tag so they load separately and in order
Add `<script src="{!$Resource.mapLibs + '/leaflet.js'}"/>` above the `ltng:require` tag
Build the `scripts` value with `join(',', $Resource.mapLibs + '/leaflet.js', $Resource.mapLibs + '/heat.js')`
Call `loadScript()` from `lightning/platformResourceLoader` in the Aura controller instead
Remove the init handler and run the map code from `afterScriptsLoaded="{!c.initMap}"` on `ltng:require`
questions.explain: Two rules fix this. Several `$Resource` references in one attribute must be combined with `join()`. And scripts load later, so code that uses them goes in `afterScriptsLoaded`, not init.
wrong: Separate `ltng:require` tags load in parallel, so `heat.js` could load before `leaflet.js`.
Aura components can't contain script tags.
`lightning/platformResourceLoader` is an LWC module; Aura uses `ltng:require`.
questions.source: Lightning Aura Components Developer Guide: Using External JavaScript Libraries

questions.q: A Lightning record page has an older Aura component that loads a charting library with `ltng:require`, and a new LWC that loads the same file with `loadScript`. Both use the same static resource URL. After the LWC renders, the Aura chart loses the plugins it had registered on the library's global object. What explains this?
options: `ltng:require` loads its scripts again each time the Aura component rerenders, which wipes the plugins it registered
Archive static resources are unpacked again on every request, which resets the global object
`ltng:require` and `loadScript` don't detect each other, so the file runs twice; load it once or check its global
Static resources with Private cache control are downloaded again for each component on the page
questions.explain: `ltng:require` and `loadScript` don't know about each other. So the same file runs twice and replaces the library's global object, plugins and all. Load it once, or have the script check for its own global first.
wrong: `ltng:require` loads each script only once, even across components.
How the zip is stored doesn't reset globals; running the script twice does.
Cache control affects server caching between users, not how often a script runs.
questions.source: Lightning Component Reference: lightning/platformResourceLoader

questions.q: A component shows a renewal record with `getRecord`. When users open it for a record they cannot access, the error banner shows up empty instead of with a message. What change fixes the banner?
options: Read `error.message` instead, because wire adapters throw standard JavaScript Error objects
Read the message from `error.statusText`, because LDS puts the message there for 4xx errors
Wrap the handler in try/catch, because wire errors are thrown instead of being passed in `error`
Check `Array.isArray(error.body)` and join the message of each item, falling back to `error.body.message`
questions.explain: UI API reads like `getRecord` give `error.body` as an **array**. Apex and write errors give an object. A `reduceErrors`-style helper handles both.
wrong: LDS errors are `FetchResponse` objects with `body`, `ok`, `status` and `statusText`, not plain Errors.
`statusText` holds status text like `NOT_FOUND`, not the message for users.
The wire passes errors in the `error` property; try/catch doesn't change the body's shape.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Handle Errors in Lightning Data Service

questions.q: A security review of a payment LWC found that when the Apex method fails, the browser receives the Apex class name and line details in `error.body.stackTrace`. The team wants users to see a short, clear message and no internal details. What should the developer do?
options: Wrap the JavaScript call in try/catch so the stack trace is not sent to the browser
Catch it in Apex and `throw new AuraHandledException('We could not apply this payment.')`
Define `PaymentException extends Exception` and throw it with the same message from a catch block
Mark the method `cacheable=true` so errors are served from the client cache without server details
questions.explain: To hide internal details, Apex must send its own message on purpose. An `AuraHandledException` returns your message, and its error has no `body.stackTrace`. Unhandled exceptions go to the client as they are.
wrong: A client try/catch runs after the browser already has the error details.
An unhandled custom exception still sends the class name and line number.
A DML method can't be cacheable, and caching doesn't hide error details anyway.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Handle Errors from Apex

questions.q: An Aura component calls an Apex method that throws `AuraHandledException('Credit limit exceeded')`. The error toast appears, but it says "undefined". What is the bug?
options: `response.getError()` returns an array, so the message is in `errors[0].message`
`AuraHandledException` sets the state to `INCOMPLETE`, so the message is never in the `ERROR` branch
The message is only available from `response.getReturnValue()` when the state is `ERROR`
`AuraHandledException` messages are only sent to Lightning web components, not to Aura components
questions.explain: In Aura, `response.getError()` returns an **array** of error objects, not one object. The `AuraHandledException` message is in `errors[0].message`. The state is still `ERROR`.
wrong: `INCOMPLETE` means the server couldn't be reached; a thrown `AuraHandledException` gives `ERROR`.
`getReturnValue()` holds a successful result, not error details.
`AuraHandledException` was built for Aura and works for LWC too.
questions.source: Lightning Aura Components Developer Guide: Returning Errors from an Apex Server-Side Controller

questions.q: On a Visualforce order page, `applyCoupon()` adds an error message when the coupon has expired. The totals panel refreshes, but users never see the error. Which two changes would show the message? (Choose 2)
questions.code:
<apex:form>
  <apex:pageMessages/>
  <apex:inputText value="{!couponCode}"/>
  <apex:commandButton value="Apply" action="{!applyCoupon}" rerender="totals"/>
  <apex:outputPanel id="totals">{!orderTotal}</apex:outputPanel>
</apex:form>

// controller
public PageReference applyCoupon() {
  if (couponIsExpired(couponCode)) {
    ApexPages.addMessage(new ApexPages.Message(
      ApexPages.Severity.ERROR, 'This coupon has expired.'));
  }
  return null;
}
options: Give `apex:pageMessages` an `id` such as `"msgs"` and set `rerender="totals,msgs"`
Add `immediate="true"` to the command button so messages are sent first
Return `new PageReference('/apex/OrderPage').setRedirect(true)` after adding the message
Change the severity to `FATAL` so the message is shown even during partial refresh
Move `apex:pageMessages` inside the totals output panel
questions.explain: A partial refresh redraws only what's in `rerender`. So the messages component must be redrawn too. Either add its id to `rerender`, or put it inside a panel that's rerendered.
wrong: `immediate` skips applying typed values, so the coupon never reaches the controller.
A redirect starts a new request, and the old messages are lost.
Severity changes the message's style, not whether it's redrawn.
questions.source: Visualforce Developer Guide: apex:pageMessages

questions.q: A partner self-registration LWC runs in an LWR Experience Cloud site. When the Apex save fails, the catch block below runs (the console log confirms it), but no toast appears on the page. What should the developer do?
options: Add `mode: 'sticky'` so the toast stays visible until it is closed
Create the event with `bubbles: true` and `composed: true` so the site shell receives it
Import `Toast` from `'lightning/toast'` and call `Toast.show({ label, message, variant: 'error' }, this)`
Add a `lightning/toastContainer` instance to the page, because `ShowToastEvent` needs a container in LWR sites
questions.explain: `lightning/platformShowToastEvent` doesn't work in LWR Experience Cloud sites. Use `lightning/toast` there. `Toast.show()` creates its own page-level toast container.
wrong: `mode` controls how long a toast stays; in an LWR site no toast shows at all.
Event travel isn't the problem; LWR sites don't handle `ShowToastEvent`.
A toast container can't make an unsupported module work in an LWR site.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Toast Notifications

questions.q: A custom two-column `lightning-record-edit-form` saves Contracts. When a validation rule blocks the save, nothing happens on screen and users think the button is broken. The team wants server errors to show in the form automatically, without writing an error handler, and must keep its custom markup (a grid with section headings and help text between the fields). A `lightning-messages` component placed just before or after the input fields
`required` on every `lightning-input-field` so errors are caught before submit
Replace the form with `lightning-record-form`, which shows errors automatically
questions.explain: The edit form can show server errors by itself if you give it a spot. Put `lightning-messages` inside `lightning-record-edit-form`. It shows save errors, validation rules included, with no handler code.
wrong: It works, but it's a custom error handler, which the team wants to avoid.
`required` only checks for empty fields in the browser; it can't catch server validation rules.
`lightning-record-form` builds its own layout, so the custom markup would be lost.
questions.source: Lightning Component Reference: lightning-record-edit-form

questions.q: A custom controller page lets users update an Account. When a validation rule (error location: top of page) fails, users get a full-page Visualforce error with `FIELD_CUSTOM_VALIDATION_EXCEPTION` instead of a friendly message on the form.
