<apex:page controller="AccountUpdateController">
  <apex:form>
    <apex:inputField value="{!account.Name}"/>
    <apex:inputField value="{!account.Rating}"/>
    <apex:commandButton value="Save" action="{!save}"/>
  </apex:form>
</apex:page>

public PageReference save() {
  update account;
  return null;
}
options: Throw `new AuraHandledException('Please fix the errors')` from `save()`
Wrap the update in `try/catch (DmlException ex)` and call `ApexPages.addMessages(ex)`
Add `<apex:pageMessages/>` (or `apex:messages`) to the page
Return `new PageReference(ApexPages.currentPage().getUrl()).setRedirect(true)` from `save()`
Set `escape="false"` on the `inputField` components so the error text can render
questions.explain: A custom controller must handle save errors itself. Catch the `DmlException` and call `ApexPages.addMessages(ex)`. Then the page needs a messages component to show top-of-page errors.
wrong: `AuraHandledException` is for Lightning components; in Visualforce it's still unhandled.
A redirect starts a new request, so the message and the user's edits are lost.
`apex:inputField` has no `escape` attribute, and escaping isn't why the error is missing.
questions.source: Visualforce Developer Guide: Validation Rules and Custom Controllers

questions.q: A related contacts LWC on the Account record page always shows "No contacts", even for accounts with many contacts. Debug logs show the Apex method runs with `accountId = 'recordId'`. What should the developer change?
options: Change the config to `{ accountId: this.recordId }`
Decorate `recordId` with `@track` as well as `@api`
Change the config to `{ accountId: '$recordId' }`
Rename the Apex parameter to `recordId` so it matches the property name
questions.explain: Without the `$`, the wire sends the literal word `'recordId'`. With `'$recordId'`, it sends the property's value. It also calls again whenever that value changes.
wrong: In a `@wire` config, `this` isn't the component, and the value wouldn't be reactive.
`@api` fields are already reactive; the problem is the literal string.
The Apex parameter must match the config key, `accountId`, which it already does.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Wire Apex Methods to Lightning Web Components

questions.q: An admin adds the "Open Cases" LWC to both the Account record page and the Home page. On the record page it works. On the Home page it shows the loading spinner forever, and no error appears in the console or the debug logs. Why?
options: The Home page has no record, so `recordId` is `undefined`, and the wire won't call Apex while a parameter is `undefined`
Apex throws a `NullPointerException` for the null Id, and cacheable methods hide server errors from the client
`@wire` only runs on record pages, so the component must call `getOpenCases` imperatively on other pages
The cached result from the record page is locked to that page, so the Home page waits until the cache entry expires
questions.explain: A wire waits while any parameter is `undefined`, and calls nothing. The Home page has no record, so `recordId` is `undefined`. No data or error ever arrives, so the spinner never stops.
wrong: Apex is never called, so there's no exception, and cacheable methods do return errors.
`@wire` works on any page; it only waits because the parameter is `undefined`.
The cache is keyed by parameters and never blocks other pages.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Wire Apex Methods to Lightning Web Components

questions.q: After a user adds a line item, the totals panel still shows the old amount until the page is reloaded. `getTotals` is `@AuraEnabled(cacheable=true)` and `addLine` is `@AuraEnabled` without cacheable. Which two changes would make the totals refresh? (Choose 2)
options: Call `refreshApex(this.totals)` after `addLine()` resolves
Mark `addLine` as `cacheable=true` so both methods share one cache entry and refresh each other
Decorate `totals` with `@track` so the template sees the new values
Remove `cacheable=true` from `getTotals` so every imperative call goes to the server
Wire `getTotals` with `{ quoteId: '$recordId' }`, keep the provisioned value, and pass it to `refreshApex()` after `addLine()` resolves
questions.explain: A cacheable method called imperatively checks the browser cache first. Same parameters can mean the same old answer. So make the call non-cacheable, or wire it and refresh with `refreshApex()`.
wrong: `refreshApex()` only works with a value a `@wire` handed over, not an imperative result.
`addLine` does DML, so it can't be cacheable.
The property is reassigned, so it's already reactive; the value itself is stale.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Client-Side Caching of Apex Method Results

questions.q: A product picker lets users tick products before adding them to a quote. Ticking a checkbox throws an "Invalid mutation ... is read-only" error in the console. What is the best fix?
options: Decorate `products` with `@track` so its nested properties can be changed
Copy the records as they arrive: `this.products = data.map((p) => ({ ...p, selected: false }))`
Call `refreshApex()` before changing the record so the wire cache is unlocked and the objects become writable
Move the assignment of `this.products` into `renderedCallback()`
questions.explain: Data from the wire service is read-only. To change it, make your own copy first. A shallow copy with an extra `selected` flag works.
wrong: `@track` doesn't make the wire's read-only objects writable.
`refreshApex()` fetches fresh data, which is read-only too.
Where you assign doesn't matter; the objects themselves are read-only.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Understand the Wire Service

questions.q: An order dashboard LWC displays the result of the Apex method below. The order number and total show correctly, but the Status column is always empty, even though debug logs show `status` is set on every object. What is the cause?
options: The `status` property is not annotated with `@AuraEnabled`, so it is not serialized to the client
Status is a restricted picklist, so it must be converted with `String.valueOf()` first
Wrapper classes must be declared `without sharing` for all their properties to be returned
The query needs `WITH USER_MODE`, otherwise picklist fields are removed from wrapper objects
questions.explain: Only Apex properties marked `@AuraEnabled` are sent to the browser. `status` lacks the annotation. So the client never gets it, and the column stays empty.
wrong: `Order.Status` is already a String in Apex; no conversion is needed.
Sharing affects which records return, not which properties are sent.
`USER_MODE` enforces permissions; it doesn't decide which wrapper properties are sent.
questions.source: Lightning Aura Components Developer Guide: Returning Data from an Apex Server-Side Controller

questions.q: Compliance wants every view of the pricing panel to be logged. A developer adds an insert to the wired Apex method below. Now the panel shows an error instead of prices. Which change meets both needs and keeps the wire?
options: Use `Database.insert(log, false)` so a failed insert does not stop the query or the wire from returning
Declare the class `without sharing` so the insert is allowed in a cacheable method
Keep `getPrices` read-only and log the view in a separate non-cacheable method called imperatively
Pass `{ cacheable: false }` in the `@wire` configuration object for this call
questions.explain: A cacheable method may only read, so it can't do DML. Keep `getPrices` read-only for the wire. Log the view in a separate non-cacheable method called imperatively.
wrong: `Database.insert` is still DML, which a cacheable method can't do.
Sharing doesn't change the no-DML rule for cacheable methods.
The wire config only passes parameters; cacheability lives on the annotation, and `@wire` needs `cacheable=true`.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Client-Side Caching of Apex Method Results

questions.q: A shipping-rate LWC uses a Continuation because the carrier API can take up to 40 seconds. The component wires `startRequest`. What happens when the component loads?
options: It works, but the response is not cached on the client
It fails to compile, because `continuation=true` and `cacheable=true` must be separated by a comma in `@AuraEnabled`
It works only for imperative calls, and the wire silently provisions nothing
It throws an exception: if the Continuation method is cacheable, the callback must be `cacheable=true` too
questions.explain: In a Continuation chain, cacheable settings must match. A cacheable starting method with a non-cacheable callback is invalid and throws an exception. Mark every method in the chain `cacheable=true` to make it work with `@wire`.
wrong: The docs list this exact combination as invalid; it doesn't just skip caching.
The attributes are separated by a space, as written: `continuation=true cacheable=true`.
The combination is invalid, so it isn't about wire versus imperative.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: @AuraEnabled Annotations for Continuations

questions.q: On a Visualforce page for Opportunity, changing Stage should redraw the forecast panel. Instead, users who have not entered a Close Date yet see "Close Date: You must enter a value" and the panel does not update. What should the developer do?
questions.code:
<apex:page standardController="Opportunity" extensions="ForecastExt">
  <apex:form>
    <apex:pageBlock id="block">
      <apex:inputField value="{!Opportunity.CloseDate}"/>
      <apex:inputField value="{!Opportunity.StageName}">
        <apex:actionSupport event="onchange" action="{!recalcForecast}" rerender="forecast"/>
      </apex:inputField>
      <apex:outputPanel id="forecast">{!forecastText}</apex:outputPanel>
    </apex:pageBlock>
  </apex:form>
</apex:page>
options: Add `immediate="true"` to the `actionSupport` so validation is skipped
Change `rerender="forecast"` to `rerender="block"` so the whole block is redrawn
Set `required="false"` on the Close Date `inputField`
Wrap the Stage `inputField` and its `actionSupport` in an `apex:actionRegion`
questions.explain: `apex:actionRegion` limits which fields the server processes in an AJAX request. Wrap Stage in it. Then only Stage is sent and checked, so the empty Close Date can't block it.
wrong: `immediate` skips validation but also drops the new Stage, so the forecast uses stale data.
`rerender` controls what's redrawn, not what's processed, so the error stays.
Close Date is required on Opportunity, and the business still needs it on save.
questions.source: Visualforce Developer Guide: apex:actionRegion

questions.q: Sales reps change the quantity, then click Recalculate. The summary panel redraws, but it still shows the totals for the old quantity. What is the cause?
questions.code:
<apex:inputText value="{!quantity}"/>
<apex:commandButton value="Recalculate" action="{!recalculate}"
                    immediate="true" rerender="summary"/>
<apex:outputPanel id="summary">Total: {!total}</apex:outputPanel>

// controller
public Integer quantity { get; set; }
public Decimal total { get; private set; }
public PageReference recalculate() {
  total = quantity * unitPrice;
  return null;
}
options: `total` has a private setter, so the page cannot show the new value
`immediate="true"` skips updating the data model, so the quantity setter never gets the new value
`rerender` only works on `apex:outputPanel` elements that also have `layout="block"`, so the panel keeps old values
`inputText` cannot bind to an Integer property; it must use `apex:inputField`
questions.explain: `immediate="true"` runs the action without saving the typed values to the controller. So `recalculate()` still sees the old quantity. `immediate` is meant for leaving actions like Cancel.
wrong: A private setter only stops the page writing `total`; the controller can still set it.
`rerender` works on any component with an id, whatever its layout.
`apex:inputText` can bind to plain properties like an Integer.
questions.source: Visualforce Developer Guide: Use the immediate Attribute Carefully

questions.q: A developer wants a Remove button on each row of an order lines table, using the markup below in a page at API version 60.0. The markup breaks a rule for `apex:actionFunction`. Which change fixes it?
questions.code: {!l.Name}
options: Replace the `actionFunction` with a `@RemoteAction` method, which can rerender the lines panel
Add `immediate="true"` to the `actionFunction` so the parameter is assigned first
Move the `apex:actionFunction` after the `apex:repeat`, still inside the `apex:form`
Move the `apex:actionFunction` outside the `apex:form` so it is defined only once
questions.explain: Since API version 23, `apex:actionFunction` can't sit inside an iteration component. Define it once after the `apex:repeat`, still inside the form. Then call it from each row with the parameter.
wrong: Remote actions are static and can't rerender Visualforce components.
`immediate` would skip applying values, and the placement problem would stay.
`apex:actionFunction` must be inside an `apex:form`.
questions.source: Visualforce Developer Guide: apex:actionFunction

questions.q: A warranty lookup button on a Visualforce page calls a slow external service that takes about 20 seconds. At month end, hundreds of agents click it at once and many get errors about too many concurrent long-running requests. What should the developer change in the controller?
options: Return a Continuation from the action, with `continuationMethod` set to a callback that reads the response
Move the callout into an `@future(callout=true)` method and set `warrantyStatus` from it
Lower `req.setTimeout()` to 5000 so each request finishes faster
Call the method with JavaScript remoting and `{ timeout: 120000 }` so the wait runs outside the page request
questions.explain: A **Continuation** hands the slow callout to a separate server and pauses the request. So it doesn't count toward the concurrent long-running request limit. A callback method reads the response when it arrives.
wrong: A future method runs later in its own transaction and can't update the waiting page.
A shorter timeout makes calls fail sooner; it doesn't speed up the service.
The server still holds the request open while it waits, so it's still long-running.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Make Long-Running Callouts with Continuations

questions.q: A tag picker shows "`{count}` selected". Users tick tags, but the count stays at 0. What should the developer change?
options: Replace `@track` with `@api` so the parent component can observe the `Set` and push its new size back down to the child
After each change, assign a new `Set`, e.g. `this.selected = new Set(this.selected)`, as `Set` mutations aren't observed
Move the `add()` and `delete()` calls into `renderedCallback()` so that every change happens inside the render cycle
Keep `@track` and add `this.selected = this.selected` after each change so the engine sees an assignment to the field
questions.explain: LWC watches plain objects and arrays, but not changes inside a `Set`, `Map`, `Date` or class instance, even with `@track`. Assigning a new `Set` gives the field a new reference. Then the component re-renders.
wrong: `@api` makes the property public and read-only to the child; it doesn't make `Set` changes visible.
Changing state in `renderedCallback` is an anti-pattern, and it still mutates the same unwatched `Set`.
Assigning the same reference equals the old value, so nothing re-renders.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Field Reactivity

questions.q: A reviewer flags the list template below. Contacts can be added and removed, and the first and last rows get special styling. What should change?
options: Use a unique value from the data as the key, such as `key={it.value.Id}`, since the index can't be a key
Move `key={it.index}` from the `li` element onto the `template` tag that holds the `iterator` directive
Replace `iterator` with `for:each`, because the `iterator` directive doesn't support `lwc:if` on its items
Replace `it.last` with a check of `it.index` against `contacts.length - 1`, because the `iterator` has no `last` property
questions.explain: Every list item needs a key: a unique string or number from the data. The docs say the index can't be the key. The iterator still gives you `value`, `index`, `first` and `last`.
wrong: The `key` goes on the first element inside the template, and an index still isn't allowed.
`lwc:if` works inside an `iterator`; `first` and `last` are why you pick `iterator`.
The iterator does offer `first` and `last` as booleans.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Render Lists

questions.q: A child LWC must round the amount its parent passes in, every time the parent changes it. The developer writes the code below, and the component fails to save. What is the fix?
options: Remove the getter, because a public property only needs a setter when the parent is the one that writes it
Rename `_amount` to `amount`, so the getter and the setter share the public property as their own backing field
Replace both with `@track amount` and do the rounding once in `connectedCallback()` when the component loads
Keep `@api` on only one of the two, by convention the getter, because a getter and setter can't both have it
questions.explain: A public property with a custom setter also needs a getter. Put `@api` on only one of them. The docs put it on the getter and keep the value in a private field like `_amount`.
wrong: A public property's setter needs a matching getter.
Using the property's own name as its store would loop into the getter and setter forever.
`connectedCallback` runs once, so later changes wouldn't be rounded, and `@track` isn't public.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Use Getters and Setters to Modify Data

questions.q: Two agents often edit the same Case in this custom LWC. The business wants a save to fail, instead of silently overwriting, if someone else saved the Case after the component loaded it. What should the developer do?
options: Call `notifyRecordUpdateAvailable([this.recordId])` just before `updateRecord`, so LDS loads the latest copy of the Case first
Add `apiName: 'Case'` to the `recordInput`, so the UI API compares record versions before it applies the update
Wire `LastModifiedDate` with `getRecord` and pass `{ ifUnmodifiedSince: lastModifiedDate }` as `updateRecord`'s `clientOptions`
Call `refreshApex` on the wired record before saving, then compare the old and new Status values in JavaScript
questions.explain: To refuse a save if someone else saved first, tell the server what version you saw. Pass `clientOptions` with `ifUnmodifiedSince` set to the `LastModifiedDate` from a wire adapter. If the record changed since, the update fails.
wrong: This refreshes the cache but still overwrites the other agent's save.
`apiName` is only for creating records; for an update, pass null or leave it out.
`refreshApex` is for wired Apex, not `getRecord`, and a JS comparison still leaves a race.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: updateRecord(recordInput, clientOptions)

questions.q: A deal summary LWC wires `getRecord` for Opportunity Amount and `CloseDate` and shows them with `getFieldValue`. Users see 125000 and 2026-12-31 instead of formatted currency and dates. The team wants formatted, localized values with no formatting code. What should the developer do?
options: Move both fields into `optionalFields`, because optional fields are returned already formatted for display to the user
Show the values with `getFieldDisplayValue(this.deal.data, AMOUNT_FIELD)`, which returns the formatted display value
Switch the wire to `layoutTypes: ['Full']`, which returns every field on the layout as a formatted string
Pass `{ formatted: true }` as a third argument to `getFieldValue`, so it returns the display value instead
questions.explain: `getFieldValue` gives the raw value; `getFieldDisplayValue` gives the formatted, localized one. Use the display version for currency and dates. The same value is also at `record.data.fields.Amount.displayValue`.
wrong: `optionalFields` only changes what happens with hidden fields; it doesn't format values.
`layoutTypes` chooses which fields come back, not whether they're formatted.
`getFieldValue` has no formatting option; `getFieldDisplayValue` is the separate function.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: getFieldDisplayValue(record, field)

questions.q: A Quick Note button in an LWC on an Account page must create a Task related to the Account with Lightning Data Service and no Apex. Which call is correct?
options: `createRecord(TASK_OBJECT, { Subject: 'Call back', WhatId: this.recordId })`
`updateRecord({ apiName: 'Task', fields: { Subject: 'Call back', WhatId: this.recordId } })`
`createRecord({ fields: { attributes: { type: 'Task' }, Subject: 'Call back', WhatId: this.recordId } })`
`createRecord({ apiName: 'Task', fields: { Subject: 'Call back', WhatId: this.recordId } })`
questions.explain: `createRecord` takes one object: the `apiName` of the object plus a `fields` map. `updateRecord` only changes existing records, found by the Id in `fields`.
wrong: `createRecord` takes one `recordInput` object, not the object and fields as separate arguments.
`updateRecord` never creates records; for an update, leave out `apiName` and include the Id.
The object is named with `apiName`, not an `attributes` block inside `fields`.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: createRecord(recordInput); updateRecord(recordInput, clientOptions)

questions.q: A Visualforce page shows only `{!opportunity.Name}` and `{!maxDiscount}`. It fails with "SObject row was retrieved via SOQL without querying the requested field: `Opportunity.Amount`". Which two changes fix it? (Choose 2)
options: Call `std.addFields(new List<String>{ 'Amount', 'Discount_Cap__c' })` in the constructor before `getRecord()`
Declare the extension `without sharing`, so the standard controller is allowed to load every field on the record
Reference both fields on the page in a hidden component, such as an `apex:outputText` with `rendered="false"`
Call `std.reset()` inside `getMaxDiscount()` just before reading the fields, so the record is queried again in full
Read the record with `std.getRecord().clone(true, true)`, because a deep clone copies every field from the database
questions.explain: A standard controller loads only the fields the page markup uses. Call `addFields()` in the constructor to load more. Or reference the fields in a hidden component (`rendered="false"`), the documented workaround.
wrong: Sharing keywords control record access, not which fields the controller loads.
`reset()` is only needed before `addFields` outside the constructor; alone it adds no fields.
`clone()` copies fields already in memory; it doesn't query new ones.
questions.source: Apex Reference Guide: StandardController Class (addFields, getRecord)

questions.q: A Visualforce mass-update page builds its `StandardSetController` from `Database.getQueryLocator` over open Cases. In a large org the query matches 14,000 Cases, and the page fails with a `LimitException`. What explains it?
options: A set controller pages at most 500 records at a time, and calling `setPageSize()` above 500 throws a `LimitException`
Query locators are capped at 50,000 rows in Visualforce, and every row also counts toward the view state
Iteration components show 1,000 rows unless `readOnly="true"`, and the overflow surfaces as a `LimitException`
The set controller handles 10,000 records; a query locator returning more throws, while a List is truncated
questions.explain: A `StandardSetController` holds at most **10,000** records. Built from a query locator that returns more, it throws a `LimitException`. Built from a bigger List, it quietly cuts it to 10,000.
wrong: There's no 500-record page size limit; the total size of the set is the problem.
The 10,000 cap applies whatever the query locator's own limit, and this isn't about view state.
The 1,000-row limit is real, but it raises a collection size error on render, not this.
questions.source: Apex Reference Guide: StandardSetController Class

questions.q: A security review flags the Visualforce page and controller below. Which risk did it find, and what is the fix?
questions.code:
<apex:page controller="CleanupController" action="{!removeContact}"/>

public with sharing class CleanupController {
    public PageReference removeContact() {
        Id cid = ApexPages.currentPage().getParameters().get('cid');
        delete [SELECT Id FROM Contact WHERE Id = :cid];
        return Page.CleanupDone;
    }
}
options: SOQL injection through the `cid` parameter; wrap it in `String.escapeSingleQuotes()` before using it in the query
CSRF: another site can send users here and the delete runs on load; delete only from a confirmed button click
XSS through `cid`; call `HTMLENCODE` on the parameter in the controller before using it in the query
Clickjacking: turn on clickjack protection for Visualforce pages, which stops the delete when the page is framed
questions.explain: A page's `action` runs on load, before any anti-CSRF token check. So a link on any site can make a signed-in user delete records: that's **CSRF**. Never do DML in a page action; require a click, like a confirm button.
wrong: The parameter is a bind variable, which is already safe from SOQL injection.
`HTMLENCODE` is an output function, and the problem is the unasked delete, not display.
Clickjack protection stops framing, but a plain link or redirect still runs the delete.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF); Secure Coding Guide

questions.q: Agents type notes with bold text and links in a rich text field. An LWC must show the formatted notes without opening an XSS hole. What should the developer use?
options: A div with `lwc:dom="manual"` whose `innerHTML` is set to the notes in `renderedCallback()`
`<lightning-formatted-rich-text value={notes}>`, which keeps allowed tags and strips the rest
A triple-brace binding such as `{{{notes}}}` in the template, so the HTML renders as markup
`<lightning-formatted-text value={notes} linkify>`, so that the HTML tags render as formatting
questions.explain: To show user HTML safely, let a component clean it first. `lightning-formatted-rich-text` keeps only allowed tags and attributes, which blocks XSS. Writing user data to `innerHTML` skips that cleaning.
wrong: `innerHTML` with user content is exactly how script injection happens.
LWC templates have no raw-HTML binding syntax.
`lightning-formatted-text` shows plain text and links; it doesn't render HTML formatting.
questions.source: Lightning Component Reference: lightning-formatted-rich-text

questions.q: A developer writes `<template lwc:if={!isLoading}>` to show results once loading ends. The component fails to compile. What is the fix?
options: Wrap the value in quotes, as in `lwc:if="{!isLoading}"`, so the compiler reads it as an expression
Bind `lwc:if={isLoaded}` to a getter returning `!this.isLoading`, as templates allow no operators
Replace `lwc:if` with `if:true={!isLoading}`, because only the older directive accepts the `!` operator
Write `lwc:if={isLoading == false}`, because templates allow comparisons but not the `!` operator
questions.explain: LWC template expressions can't contain operators: no `!`, no `==`, no `&&`. Put the logic in a JavaScript getter and bind to it. Or use `lwc:if={isLoading}` with `lwc:else`.
wrong: `{!...}` is Aura syntax, and LWC doesn't allow `!` in any form.
`if:true` doesn't accept `!` either.
Comparisons are operators too, so they aren't allowed.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Data Binding in a Template; Render HTML Conditionally

questions.q: A parent LWC contains one child. Both log from their `constructor()`, `connectedCallback()` and `renderedCallback()`. In which order do the `connectedCallback()` and `renderedCallback()` logs appear?
options: `connectedCallback()`: child, then parent. `renderedCallback()`: parent, then child
Both hooks run in the parent first, then the child, since rendering flows down the tree
Both hooks run in the child first, then the parent, since a parent waits for its children
`connectedCallback()`: parent, then child. `renderedCallback()`: child, then parent
questions.explain: Setup flows down the tree, and finishing flows up. `connectedCallback()` runs in the parent before the child. `renderedCallback()` runs in the child first, because the parent is done only when its children are.
wrong: It's the other way round for both hooks.
`renderedCallback()` flows up, from child to parent.
`connectedCallback()` flows down, from parent to child.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Lifecycle Flow

questions.q: A component's template has `<canvas lwc:ref="chart"></canvas>`. Its `connectedCallback()` calls `this.refs.chart.getContext('2d')` and throws a `TypeError`. What should the developer do?
options: Use `this.template.querySelector('canvas')` instead, which does work in `connectedCallback()`
Add `lwc:dom="manual"` to the canvas, because refs work only on elements you add yourself
Move it to `renderedCallback()`, after the template renders, with a guard so it runs once
Call `this.refs.chart` in the `constructor()`, because refs exist before the component connects
questions.explain: In `connectedCallback()`, the template hasn't rendered yet, so the canvas doesn't exist. Use the ref in `renderedCallback()`. That hook runs after every render, so use a flag to set up the chart once.
wrong: `querySelector()` has the same problem; nothing has rendered yet.
`lwc:dom="manual"` is for DOM you add by hand, not for refs.
The constructor runs even earlier, before anything renders.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Access Elements the Component Owns (refs); Lifecycle Hooks

questions.q: A search bar shows only a `lightning-input` and a magnifier icon, with no visible label. An accessibility audit says screen readers announce it as an unlabeled edit field. What should the developer do?
options: Set `label="Search accounts"` with `variant="label-hidden"`, so the label is read but not shown
Set `placeholder="Search accounts"`, because screen readers treat a placeholder as the label
Wrap it in a `<div title="Search accounts">`, so the tooltip names the field for screen readers
Add `aria-hidden="true"` to the icon only, so screen readers name the field from the icon
questions.explain: Every input needs a real label, even if you don't show it. Set `label`, then hide it visually with `variant="label-hidden"`. Screen readers still read it, and a placeholder is no substitute.
wrong: Placeholders disappear as you type and aren't a reliable label.
A title on a wrapper doesn't label the input inside.
Hiding the icon removes noise but still leaves the field unnamed.
questions.source: Lightning Component Library: lightning-input (Accessibility); LWC Developer Guide: Accessibility

questions.q: A row of icon-only `lightning-button-icon` buttons (Edit, Delete) fails an accessibility review. Each row's status is also shown only as a red or green dot. Which two fixes are correct? (Choose 2)
options: Add `title` attributes to the dots, and keep color as the only visible signal
Give each button an `alternative-text` value, such as `alternative-text="Delete"`
Set `tabindex="-1"` on the buttons, so screen readers skip them and read the row
Add `aria-live="assertive"` to each button, so its name is read when the page loads
Show the status as text or an icon too, so color isn't the only way to tell
questions.explain: Icon-only buttons need text a screen reader can say, and `alternative-text` gives it. Color alone fails people who can't tell colors apart. Add a word or a shape next to the dot.
wrong: A tooltip helps a little, but color is still the only thing most people see.
That takes the buttons out of keyboard reach.
Live regions announce changes; they don't name buttons.
questions.source: Lightning Component Library: lightning-button-icon; Lightning Design System: Accessibility

questions.q: This picker never receives any values for `Industry`. What is missing?
options: An `objectApiName: 'Account'` value, because `fieldApiName` alone doesn't name the object
The `@track` decorator on `industries`, because wired results aren't reactive on their own
A `recordTypeId`, such as `'$objectInfo.data.defaultRecordTypeId'` from `getObjectInfo`
A call to `refreshApex(this.industries)` in `connectedCallback()` to load the first values
questions.explain: Picklist values can differ by record type, so `getPicklistValues` needs a `recordTypeId`. Get it from `getObjectInfo`, often its `defaultRecordTypeId`. Pass it with `$` so the wire waits for it.
wrong: The field import already names the object; the record type is missing.
Wired properties are already reactive.
`refreshApex()` is for Apex wires, and it can't add a missing parameter.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: getPicklistValues

questions.q: A Mark Done button runs `updateRecord({ fields: { Status__c: 'Done' } })`. The promise rejects every time. What is wrong?
options: `updateRecord` needs an `apiName` value too, like `createRecord`, to know the object to update
The `fields` object must include the record's `Id`, so the call knows which record to update
`updateRecord` works only inside a `lightning-record-edit-form`, not in a click handler
Field names must be schema imports; plain strings like `Status__c` are always rejected
questions.explain: `updateRecord` finds the record by the `Id` inside `fields`. Without it, there's nothing to update. Use `fields: { Id: this.recordId, Status__c: 'Done' }`.
wrong: `apiName` belongs to `createRecord`; updates use the `Id`.
It's a JavaScript function you can call from any handler.
Strings work; imports just add checks when you save.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: updateRecord

questions.q: An LWC on the Account record page must list the account's Contacts with Name and Email, using Lightning Data Service and no Apex. Which wire is correct?
options: `@wire(getRecord, { recordId: '$recordId', fields: ['Account.Contacts.Name', 'Account.Contacts.Email', 'Account.Id'] })`
`@wire(getRelatedListRecords, { recordId: 'recordId', relatedListId: 'Contact', fields: ['Name', 'Email', 'Id'] })`
`@wire(getListUi, { objectApiName: 'Contact', parentRecordId: '$recordId', fields: ['Name', 'Email'] })`
`@wire(getRelatedListRecords, { parentRecordId: '$recordId', relatedListId: 'Contacts', fields: ['Contact.Name', 'Contact.Email'] })`
questions.explain: `getRelatedListRecords` from `lightning/uiRelatedListApi` reads one related list. It needs `parentRecordId`, the list's Id (`Contacts`) and fields named `Object.Field`. Use `$recordId` so the wire reacts.
wrong: `getRecord` can't read a child list through `Account.Contacts`.
The key is `parentRecordId`, the Id needs `$`, and the list is `Contacts`.
`getListUi` reads list views, not related lists.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: getRelatedListRecords

questions.q: In a record page LWC, `@wire(getRecord, { recordId: 'recordId', fields: FIELDS })` always returns an error, though `this.recordId` holds the right value. What is wrong?
options: `'recordId'` is plain text; it must be `'$recordId'` so the wire reads the property
`recordId` must use `@track`, because an `@api` property can't feed a wire adapter
`FIELDS` must move to `optionalFields`, because `fields` fails for record page wires
`getRecord` can't run on record pages, so it must use `CurrentPageReference` instead
questions.explain: In a wire's config, a string that starts with `$` points to a property. Without the `$`, the adapter gets the literal text `recordId`, which isn't an Id. With `'$recordId'`, the wire also reruns when the Id changes.
wrong: `@api` properties work fine as reactive wire parameters.
`fields` works on record pages; the Id is the problem.
`getRecord` is made for record pages.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Understand the Wire Service (reactive parameters)

questions.q: A team picks between `lightning-record-form`, `lightning-record-edit-form` and `lightning-record-view-form`. Which two statements are true? (Choose 2)
options: `lightning-record-form` can show a full or compact layout without listing each field
`lightning-record-form` lets you place each field yourself with `lightning-input-field`
`lightning-record-view-form` edits a field inline when the user double-clicks on it
`lightning-record-edit-form` lets you change field values in `onsubmit` before saving
All three forms ignore field-level security, so the component must hide fields itself
questions.explain: `lightning-record-form` is the quickest: give it a layout type or a field list. `lightning-record-edit-form` gives you control: your own layout and an `onsubmit` hook. All three respect field-level security.
wrong: That's `lightning-record-edit-form`; `lightning-record-form` lays out fields itself.
`lightning-record-view-form` is read-only.
All three respect field-level security.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Compare Base Components for Forms

questions.q: Two LWCs on an Opportunity record page both wire `getRecord` for the same record. One saves a new Stage with `updateRecord`. What happens in the other component?
options: It keeps the old Stage until it calls `refreshApex()` on its own wired `getRecord` value
It gets the new Stage itself, since both read from one Lightning Data Service cache
It keeps the old Stage until a reload, because each component holds a private record cache
It gets the new Stage only if both components import the field through the same schema path
questions.explain: Lightning Data Service keeps one shared cache per record. A change made with `updateRecord` updates that cache. Every component wired to that record gets the new value.
wrong: `refreshApex()` is for Apex wires, and LDS updates without it.
Components share one LDS cache, not private ones.
Any field import for the same field reads the same cache.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Lightning Data Service

questions.q: A type-ahead LWC calls an imperative Apex search on every keystroke. Fast typists cause many server calls and slow results. What is the recommended fix?
options: Make the method `cacheable=true` and wire it, since wired calls never hit the server for new text
Call the Apex method from `renderedCallback()`, which batches all keystrokes into a single call
Wait about 300 ms after the last key with `setTimeout`, clearing the old timer, then call Apex
Use `Promise.all()` to send all the keystrokes' calls together in one network round trip
questions.explain: Don't call the server for every key. **Debounce**: start a short timer on each keystroke and clear the old one. Only the last timer fires, so you make one call when the user pauses.
wrong: New search text still means a new server call, wired or not.
`renderedCallback()` doesn't batch anything; it runs after each render.
`Promise.all()` still sends every call.
questions.source: LWC Recipes (GitHub): apexImperativeMethodWithParams; LWC Developer Guide: Performance

questions.q: A `lightning-datatable` must let users browse up to 50,000 Cases. Loading all of them at once is very slow. Which approach fits best?
options: Load every row with one `cacheable=true` call, because cached Apex results skip the heap size limit
Use `for:each` over all the rows inside `lightning-layout`, which draws only the rows on screen
Return all rows from an `@AuraEnabled` method marked `@ReadOnly`, which lifts the query limits
Set `enable-infinite-loading` and handle `onloadmore` to fetch the next page of rows as users scroll
questions.explain: Load data in pages, not all at once. With `enable-infinite-loading`, the table fires `onloadmore` near the bottom. Fetch the next batch then, and set `isLoading` while it loads.
wrong: Caching doesn't lift the heap limit, and the browser still gets every row.
`for:each` draws every row; it doesn't skip hidden ones.
`@ReadOnly` doesn't apply to `@AuraEnabled` methods, and the page would still choke.
questions.source: Lightning Component Library: lightning-datatable (Loading More Data)

questions.q: An LWC runs `getCases({ accId: this.recordId })`. The Apex method is `public static List<Case> getCases(Id accountId)`, and inside it `accountId` is always `null`. What should change?
options: Rename the key to `accountId`, because the object's keys must match the Apex parameter names
Pass the Id as a plain value, `getCases(this.recordId)`, because imperative calls use position
Change the parameter type to `String`, since an `Id` can't be passed from JavaScript to Apex
Add `cacheable=true`, because methods without it receive parameters only when they are wired
questions.explain: Apex parameters are matched by name, not by position. The JavaScript object's keys must match the parameter names. Here `accId` doesn't match `accountId`, so `accountId` stays `null`.
wrong: Imperative calls take one object of named values, not positions.
An Id string passes to an `Id` parameter just fine.
Parameters reach non-cacheable methods too.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Call Apex Methods Imperatively

questions.q: A record page LWC is slow to open. It loads a 2 MB charting library and renders a chart tab that most users never open. Which two changes improve load time? (Choose 2)
options: Paste the library into the component's own JavaScript file, so no extra file loads
Hide the chart with CSS `display: none`, which stops the child from being created
Render the chart tab's child component with `lwc:if` only once the tab is opened
Mark every Apex method `cacheable=false`, so the browser skips all its cache lookups
Load the library with `loadScript()` the first time the chart is shown, not on load
questions.explain: Do less work until the user needs it. `lwc:if` doesn't create the chart component until the tab opens. Loading the library at that moment too keeps the first load light.
wrong: Inlining still downloads the same 2 MB on every load.
Hidden elements are still created and rendered.
Turning off caching makes loading slower, not faster.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Performance Best Practices; Use Third-Party JavaScript Libraries

questions.q: A delete button uses `if (window.confirm('Delete?'))`. In Chrome the prompt no longer appears in Lightning Experience, and nothing gets deleted. What should the developer use?
options: `ShowToastEvent` with variant `warning`, then delete when the user closes the toast message
`LightningConfirm.open()` from `lightning/confirm`, then delete if the promise gives `true`
`window.top.confirm()`, which reaches past the cross-origin frame that blocks the dialog box
`this.template.confirm()`, the component-scoped version of the browser dialog in Lightning
questions.explain: Chrome blocks native dialogs like `confirm()` in cross-origin frames. `LightningConfirm.open()` shows a Lightning modal instead. It returns a promise that resolves to `true` or `false`.
wrong: A toast isn't a question, and closing it doesn't mean yes.
Reaching the top window from a Lightning frame is blocked and unsupported.
There's no `template.confirm()` method.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: lightning/confirm (LightningConfirm)

questions.q: A form must show "End date must be after start date" under the End Date `lightning-input` when the dates are wrong. Which code does that?
options: `endInput.messageWhenBadInput = 'End date must be after start date'; endInput.focus();`
`this.dispatchEvent(new ShowToastEvent({ message: 'End date must be after start date' }));`
`endInput.validity.valid = false; endInput.errorMessage = 'End date must be after start date';`
`endInput.setCustomValidity('End date must be after start date'); endInput.reportValidity();`
questions.explain: `setCustomValidity()` sets your own error message on the field. `reportValidity()` then shows it right under the input. Pass an empty string later to clear it.
wrong: `messageWhenBadInput` covers only the built-in bad-input check, not your own rule.
A toast shows away from the field and then goes away.
`validity` is read-only, and there's no `errorMessage` property.
questions.source: Lightning Component Library: lightning-input (Custom Validity)

questions.q: A team is writing error-handling guidelines for LWCs and their Apex controllers. Which two guidelines match Salesforce best practices? (Choose 2)
options: Send `e.getStackTraceString()` to the browser, so users can report the failing Apex line
Throw `AuraHandledException` in Apex with a message that is safe and useful for users
Use `console.error()` as the only feedback, because toasts interrupt users during errors
Show a field's own error next to it with `setCustomValidity()` and `reportValidity()`
Catch each error in the `errorCallback()` of the same component that threw it, then show a fallback
questions.explain: Users need clear, safe messages close to the problem. `AuraHandledException` sends your chosen message to the client without internal details. Field errors belong next to the field.
wrong: Stack traces leak internal details and don't help users.
Users don't see the browser console.
`errorCallback()` catches errors from child components, not from its own component.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Handle Errors; Apex Reference Guide: AuraHandledException

questions.q: A child LWC reads `this.label` in its `constructor()` to build a heading. The parent sets `label="Orders"`, but the heading is always empty. Where should the code read `label`?
options: In the `constructor()` after calling `super()` twice, so the parent's values are copied in
In `disconnectedCallback()`, which runs once the parent has passed in all of its properties
In `connectedCallback()` or a getter; public properties are set after the constructor
In `errorCallback()`, because reading a public property in the constructor raises an error
questions.explain: The constructor runs before the parent sets public properties. So `this.label` is still empty there. Read it in `connectedCallback()`, or better, in a getter that always uses the current value.
wrong: `super()` is called once, and that doesn't bring in public properties.
`disconnectedCallback()` runs when the component is removed.
Nothing is thrown; the value just isn't set yet.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Lifecycle Hooks (constructor)

questions.q: In `c-order-list`, a `<div onpick={handlePick}>` wraps many `<c-order-row>` elements. When a row's button is clicked, the row runs `this.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('pick', { bubbles: true }))`. How does `handlePick` know which row fired?
options: `event.target` is the `c-order-row` that fired, so read its `@api` values or `dataset`
`event.target` is the `<button>` inside the row, so read the button's `data-id` attribute
`event.target` is always the `<div>` that has the listener, so the row must send `detail`
`event.target` is `null` for custom events, so the row must call a method on the list
questions.explain: The row dispatches from `this`, so the event's target is the row's host element. The button lives in the row's shadow DOM, which the list can't see. So `event.target` is the `c-order-row`.
wrong: The button sits in the row's shadow tree, and the event was fired on the row.
That's `event.currentTarget`; `target` is the element that fired.
Custom events have a target like any other event.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Event Retargeting; Configure Event Propagation

questions.q: `c-wizard` wants one listener for `step` events fired by child components in its own template. Its `connectedCallback()` runs `this.addEventListener('step', this.handleStep)`. Children dispatch with `bubbles: true` only. Why does the handler never run?
options: Use `window.addEventListener('step', ...)`, because only the window hears events from children
Move the call into the `constructor()`, because listeners added after connecting are ignored
Use `this.template.addEventListener('step', ...)`, since the event stops at the shadow root
Dispatch with `bubbles: false`, because `this.addEventListener` skips events that bubble
questions.explain: `this.template` is the component's shadow root, where its own children live. A bubbling event that isn't `composed` stops at that shadow root. So listen on `this.template`; `this` only hears events that reach the host.
wrong: The event never leaves the shadow tree, so the window never hears it.
Listeners added in `connectedCallback()` work fine.
Without bubbling, the event never leaves the child at all.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Handle Events (Attach Event Listeners Programmatically); Configure Event Propagation

questions.q: A team uses Lightning Message Service to share a selected product between components on a Lightning page. Which two statements are true? (Choose 2)
options: An LWC gets the context with `@wire(MessageContext)`, then calls `subscribe()` with it
Messages reach components in any browser tab where the same user has Lightning open
Visualforce pages and Aura components can publish and subscribe on the same channel
A channel is created at runtime by the first component that calls `publish()` on it
Apex triggers can call `publish()` to send messages straight to the open components
questions.explain: LMS links components on one Lightning page, across LWC, Aura and Visualforce. A channel is `LightningMessageChannel` metadata that you deploy. In LWC, get the context with `@wire(MessageContext)`, then `publish()` or `subscribe()`.
wrong: LMS works within one browser tab, not across tabs.
Channels are metadata you deploy, not runtime objects.
LMS is client-side; Apex can't publish to it.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Communicate Across the DOM with Lightning Message Service

questions.q: A child LWC dispatches `new CustomEvent('change', { detail: this.filters })`, where `filters` is an object. A parent edits `event.detail.status`, and the child's filters change unexpectedly. What is the best practice?
options: Mark `filters` with `@api`, which makes that object read-only for every listener it reaches
Send primitives or a copy, like `detail: { ...this.filters }`, to keep the child's data safe
Set `composed: true` on the event, which passes `detail` to listeners as a frozen deep copy
Use `@track` on `filters`, which makes the framework send a fresh copy on each dispatch
questions.explain: `detail` passes objects by reference, so a listener can change the sender's data. Send primitive values, or a copy of the object. Then each side owns its own data.
wrong: `@api` is for values a parent passes down, not for event payloads.
`composed` controls how far the event travels, not copying.
`@track` watches changes; it doesn't copy the payload.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Event Best Practices

questions.q: A Recalculate quick action on Opportunity must run logic with no modal. The LWC's `js-meta.xml` uses target `lightning__RecordAction` with `<actionType>Action</actionType>`. What must the JavaScript provide?
options: A `connectedCallback()` that runs the logic, then a `CloseActionScreenEvent` to close
A `render()` method that returns `null`, so the action shows no modal while it runs
An `@api recordId` setter that runs the logic, as headless actions call only setters
A public `invoke()` method, marked `@api`, which runs when the user clicks the action
questions.explain: A headless quick action, with `actionType` `Action`, shows no UI. Salesforce calls the component's `@api invoke()` method when the user clicks. The method can still use `@api recordId`.
wrong: Headless actions run `invoke()`; `CloseActionScreenEvent` is for screen actions.
`render()` picks a template; it doesn't make an action headless.
The setter isn't the entry point; `invoke()` is.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Create Headless Quick Actions

questions.q: Admins must pick a Region for a component in Lightning App Builder. The list of regions comes from a custom metadata type. Which setup works?
options: A `<property>` with `datasource="apex://RegionPicklist"`, a class extending `VisualEditor.DynamicPickList`
A `<property>` with `type="Picklist"` and `values="{!Region__mdt}"`, which reads the records at design time
An `@api regions` property filled by `@wire(getPicklistValues)` that App Builder reads when it opens
A `<property>` with `datasource="Region__mdt"`, which lists all of that type's records in App Builder
questions.explain: App Builder can fill a property's list from Apex. Point `datasource` at `apex://ClassName`, where the class extends `VisualEditor.DynamicPickList`. It returns the default value and the list of values.
wrong: There's no `Picklist` type or merge field like that in `js-meta.xml`.
App Builder doesn't read wired values; and the regions aren't a picklist field.
`datasource` takes a list of values or an `apex://` class, not an object name.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Component Configuration Tags (datasource); Apex Reference: VisualEditor.DynamicPickList

questions.q: A New Case button in an LWC must open the standard New Case form with Origin already set to Web. Which page reference does that?
options: `standard__recordPage` with `actionName: 'new'` and `attributes: { Origin: 'Web' }`, which pre-fills the new record
`standard__objectPage` for Case, `actionName: 'new'`, and `defaultFieldValues` from `encodeDefaultFieldValues()` in `state`
`standard__objectPage` for Case, `actionName: 'new'`, and `state: { c__Origin: 'Web' }`, which the standard form reads
`standard__webPage` with the URL `/lightning/o/Case/new?Origin=Web`, so that the form reads the query parameter
questions.explain: To pre-fill a standard New form, navigate to the object page with `actionName: 'new'`. Put the values in `state.defaultFieldValues`. Build that string with `encodeDefaultFieldValues()` from `lightning/pageReferenceUtils`.
wrong: A record page shows an existing record, and attributes don't set fields.
`c__` state is for your own components; the standard form reads `defaultFieldValues`.
A plain query parameter like `Origin=Web` isn't read by the form.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Navigate to a Record Create Page with Default Field Values

questions.q: A component must be draggable in Experience Builder, with a Title property that site admins can set there. Which `js-meta.xml` setup is correct?
options: Target `lightning__AppPage` only, because Experience Builder lists every App Builder component
Target `lightningCommunity__Page` only, with the `<property>` inside that target's own `targetConfig`
Targets `lightningCommunity__Page` and `lightningCommunity__Default`, with the property in `Default`
Targets `lightning__CommunityPage` and `lightning__HomePage`, with `<isExposed>false</isExposed>`
questions.explain: `lightningCommunity__Page` puts the component in Experience Builder. Properties that admins set there go in a `targetConfig` for `lightningCommunity__Default`. The component also needs `<isExposed>true</isExposed>`.
wrong: App page targets don't make a component show in Experience Builder.
Properties for Experience Builder go in the `lightningCommunity__Default` config.
Those target names are wrong, and the component must be exposed.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Configure a Component for Experience Builder

questions.q: A flow screen LWC must move to the next screen as soon as the user picks a warehouse, without the user clicking Next. What should it do?
options: Dispatch `new FlowAttributeChangeEvent('next', true)`, which tells the flow to move ahead
Call `this[NavigationMixin.Navigate]` with type `standard__flowScreen` and `actionName: 'next'`
Fire `new CustomEvent('next', { bubbles: true, composed: true })`, which the flow handles
Check that `availableActions` includes `'NEXT'`, then dispatch `new FlowNavigationNextEvent()`
questions.explain: Flow screens give components navigation events in `lightning/flowSupport`. Declare `@api availableActions`, check that it contains `'NEXT'`, then dispatch `FlowNavigationNextEvent`. The flow moves on.
wrong: That event updates an output value; it doesn't navigate.
There's no `standard__flowScreen` page type.
The flow runtime doesn't listen for a custom `next` event.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Flow Screen Components (Navigation Events)

questions.q: An Aura component must be placeable on Account record pages in Lightning App Builder and must read the current record's Id. Which two interfaces should it implement? (Choose 2)
options: `force:appHostable`
`lightning:isUrlAddressable`
`flexipage:availableForAllPageTypes` only, which also passes in `recordId`
`flexipage:availableForRecordHome`
`force:hasRecordId`
questions.explain: `flexipage:availableForRecordHome` lets App Builder place the component on record pages. `force:hasRecordId` gives it the record's Id in `v.recordId`. You need both.
wrong: That makes a component usable as a custom tab.
That lets a component open from a URL; it doesn't add it to pages.
That puts it on any page but doesn't pass the record Id.
questions.source: Lightning Aura Components Developer Guide: Configure Components for Lightning Experience Record Pages

questions.q: An Aura component updates `v.status` inside a `setTimeout` callback. The value changes, but the view doesn't redraw until the user clicks something. What is the fix?
options: Wrap the callback in `$A.getCallback()`, so it runs inside the Aura lifecycle
Call `component.rerender()` right after `component.set()` in the callback to force a redraw
Replace `setTimeout` with `window.requestAnimationFrame()`, which Aura always watches
Move the code into the renderer's `afterRender` function, which Aura reruns after timers
questions.explain: Code that runs outside Aura's own flow, like a `setTimeout` or a third-party callback, must be wrapped. `$A.getCallback()` brings it back into the framework's lifecycle. Then Aura sees the change and redraws.
wrong: Forcing a redraw isn't the supported fix; the change happened outside Aura.
Aura doesn't watch animation frames any more than timers.
`afterRender` runs after a render, not after timers.
questions.source: Lightning Aura Components Developer Guide: Modifying Components Outside the Framework Lifecycle

questions.q: An Aura component calls `getRegions`, an `@AuraEnabled(cacheable=true)` Apex method, every time it loads. The list rarely changes. How can it show cached results right away?
options: Call `action.setBackground()`, which saves the response in the browser for later page loads
Call `action.setStorable()` before `$A.enqueueAction(action)`, so the client cache can answer
Store the list in an `aura:attribute` with `access="global"`, which keeps it across page loads
Call `action.setAbortable()`, which keeps the last response for the next time the page loads
questions.explain: In Aura, a storable action can be answered from the client cache. Mark the Apex method `cacheable=true` and call `action.setStorable()`. The cached response shows fast, and a fresh one can follow.
wrong: Background actions change queue priority, not caching.
`access` controls who can use the attribute, not how long it lasts.
Abortable actions can be cancelled; they don't cache.
questions.source: Lightning Aura Components Developer Guide: Storable Actions

questions.q: An Aura component must react every time its `v.accountId` attribute changes, including when the parent sets it later. Which markup fits?
options: `<aura:handler name="init" value="{!v.accountId}" action="{!c.onIdChange}"/>`
`<aura:handler event="aura:doneRendering" action="{!c.onIdChange}"/>` on its own
`<aura:attribute name="accountId" type="Id" onchange="{!c.onIdChange}"/>`
`<aura:handler name="change" value="{!v.accountId}" action="{!c.onIdChange}"/>`
questions.explain: In Aura, a `change` handler watches one attribute. Set `name="change"` and point `value` at `{!v.accountId}`. The `init` handler runs only once, when the component starts.
wrong: `init` runs once at startup, not on later changes.
That event fires after rendering, not when one attribute changes.
`aura:attribute` has no `onchange` attribute.
questions.source: Lightning Aura Components Developer Guide: Detecting Data Changes with Change Handlers

questions.q: A Visualforce page uses a custom controller to show and edit Opportunities. A security review asks which permissions apply. Which two statements are true? (Choose 2)
options: A custom controller always enforces the user's field-level security in every SOQL query it runs
A standard controller respects the user's object permissions, field-level security and sharing
A custom controller runs in system mode, and sharing applies only if the class is `with sharing`
Adding a controller extension switches a standard controller page to system mode for every action
`<apex:inputField>` ignores field-level security on pages that use a custom controller
questions.explain: Standard controllers run in user mode, so object, field and record access all apply. Custom controllers and extensions run in system mode. Use `with sharing` for record access, and check fields yourself.
wrong: Custom controller queries run in system mode unless you add checks.
Extension methods run in system mode, but standard actions still run in user mode.
Components bound to fields, like `apex:inputField`, still respect field-level security.
questions.source: Visualforce Developer Guide: Security of Custom Controllers and Controller Extensions

questions.q: A three-page Visualforce wizard shares one custom controller. Step 1 calls the `next()` method below. On step 2, the values entered on step 1 are gone. Which line causes this?
options: `Page.WizardStep2`, because wizard pages must be opened with `new PageReference('/apex/...')`
`return p;`, because the method must return `null` so that the state is kept between pages
`p.setRedirect(true);`, because a client redirect starts a new request and drops view state
`public PageReference next()`, because wizard actions must be `static` to keep values around
questions.explain: With `setRedirect(true)`, the browser makes a fresh request, so the controller and view state start over. With `false`, and the same controller on both pages, the view state carries over. That's how wizards keep data.
wrong: Both forms point to the same page; the redirect flag is the issue.
Returning `null` keeps the user on step 1.
Static members aren't kept in view state at all.
questions.source: Visualforce Developer Guide: Creating a Wizard; Apex Reference: PageReference.setRedirect

questions.q: A Visualforce custom controller logs each visit by inserting a `Page_Visit__c` record in its constructor. The page fails with "DML currently not allowed". What should the developer do?
options: Move the insert into a method named in the page's `action` attribute, which may run DML
Mark the constructor `@future`, so that the insert runs later in its own separate transaction
Use `Database.insert(visit, false)`, which is allowed in constructors because it doesn't throw
Move the insert into the getter of a property the page shows, since getters run after load
questions.explain: Visualforce doesn't allow DML in a controller's constructor or getters. Put it in an action method, like one set in `<apex:page action="{!logVisit}">`. Keep page actions to safe work like logging, because they run on load.
wrong: Constructors can't be `@future`.
The rule blocks all DML there, whatever the method.
Getters can't run DML either.
questions.source: Visualforce Developer Guide: Custom Controllers (DML restrictions); apex:page action attribute

questions.q: A developer writes an extension for `<apex:page standardController="Case" extensions="CaseExt">`. Which constructor must `CaseExt` have?
options: `public CaseExt(Case record)`
`public CaseExt(ApexPages.StandardSetController ctrl)`
`public CaseExt(ApexPages.StandardController ctrl)`
`public CaseExt()` with no arguments
questions.explain: An extension of a standard controller gets that controller passed in. So it needs a constructor that takes one `ApexPages.StandardController`. From it, `getRecord()` returns the Case.
wrong: The page passes the controller, not the record.
`StandardSetController` is for pages with `recordSetVar`.
A no-argument constructor is for custom controllers.
questions.source: Visualforce Developer Guide: Building a Controller Extension

questions.q: A Visualforce form has several required fields. Its Cancel button calls `cancelEdit()`, but users who leave required fields empty see "You must enter a value" and can't leave. What should the developer do?
options: Add `rerender="none"` to the Cancel button, so the form isn't sent before `cancelEdit()` runs
Add `immediate="true"` to the Cancel button, which skips validation and doesn't apply values
Wrap the required fields in an `apex:actionRegion`, which skips them for every page button
Set `required="false"` on every field when Cancel is clicked, with an `onclick` handler
questions.explain: `immediate="true"` runs the action without validating or saving the form's values. That's what Cancel needs. An `actionRegion` limits what is sent for actions inside it, not for buttons elsewhere.
wrong: A rerender still sends and validates the form.
Buttons outside the region still send the whole form.
Client-side tricks don't change server-side validation.
questions.source: Visualforce Developer Guide: apex:commandButton (immediate attribute)

questions.q: A Search button rerenders a results panel after a slow query. Users click it several times because nothing shows that the search is running. What should the developer add?
options: An `apex:actionPoller` that checks every second whether the search has finished yet
An `apex:pageMessages` component, which shows a progress bar while any action runs
An `apex:outputPanel` with `layout="block"` around the button, which disables it while busy
An `apex:actionStatus` with "Searching…" text, named in the button's `status` attribute
questions.explain: `apex:actionStatus` shows something while an AJAX request runs, like a spinner or text. Point the button's `status` attribute at it. Then users can see the search is working.
wrong: A poller sends more requests and shows no progress.
Page messages show errors and info, not progress.
An output panel just groups markup; it disables nothing.
questions.source: Visualforce Developer Guide: apex:actionStatus

questions.q: An upload page has `<apex:inputFile value="{!doc.Body}"/>` and an `apex:commandButton` with `rerender="msgs"`. Clicking Upload fails with an error about `apex:inputFile`. What is the fix?
options: Remove `rerender` from the button, because `apex:inputFile` can't be used with a rerendering action
Move the `apex:inputFile` into an `apex:actionRegion`, which allows file uploads during rerenders
Add `enctype="multipart/form-data"` to the `apex:commandButton`, which turns on AJAX file posts
Mark `doc` as `transient`, because files can't be kept in view state during a partial refresh
questions.explain: A file upload needs a full page post, not a partial AJAX refresh. So `apex:inputFile` can't work with a button that uses `rerender`. Drop `rerender` and let the page reload.
wrong: An action region doesn't make AJAX posts carry files.
Buttons have no `enctype`; and the AJAX request still can't send the file.
`transient` helps view state size, but the error is about `rerender`.
questions.source: Visualforce Developer Guide: apex:inputFile

questions.q: A `@RemoteAction` method can take up to 90 seconds. Calls from the page fail after 30 seconds. How should the page call it?
options: Add `@RemoteAction(timeout=90)` to the Apex method, since the server sets the time limit
Pass `{ timeout: 120000 }` in the config of `Visualforce.remoting.Manager.invokeAction()`
Pass `{ buffer: false }` in the call's config, which turns off the 30-second time limit
Split the work into `@future` methods, as remoting calls can never run past 30 seconds
questions.explain: Remoting requests time out after 30 seconds by default. Set the `timeout` option in the call's config, up to 120,000 ms. That covers a 90-second call.
wrong: `@RemoteAction` has no timeout setting.
`buffer` controls grouping of requests, not the timeout.
The limit can be raised to 120 seconds.
questions.source: Visualforce Developer Guide: Configuring JavaScript Remoting Requests

questions.q: A Visualforce page has `<button onclick="greet('{!$CurrentPage.parameters.name}')">`. Which encoding fixes the XSS risk in this spot?
options: `{!HTMLENCODE($CurrentPage.parameters.name)}`, because the value sits inside an HTML tag
`{!URLENCODE($CurrentPage.parameters.name)}`, because the value came in through the URL
`{!JSINHTMLENCODE($CurrentPage.parameters.name)}`, for JavaScript in an HTML attribute
`{!JSENCODE($CurrentPage.parameters.name)}`, because only JavaScript runs on the click
questions.explain: Pick the encoding for where the value lands. Here it's JavaScript inside an HTML attribute, so use `JSINHTMLENCODE`. `JSENCODE` alone suits a `<script>` block, not an `onclick` attribute.
wrong: HTML encoding alone doesn't make the value safe inside JavaScript.
URL encoding is for values placed in links.
In an attribute, the browser HTML-decodes first, so `JSENCODE` alone isn't enough.
questions.source: Secure Coding Guide: Cross-Site Scripting (Visualforce encoding functions)

questions.q: A security review flags this method, which a search LWC calls with the user's text. What is the best fix?
options: Encode `term` in the LWC with `encodeURIComponent()` before sending it to the Apex method
Add `with sharing` to the class, which stops injected filters from reading extra records
Mark the method `cacheable=false`, because cacheable methods can't check their inputs
Bind it: set `String pattern = '%' + term + '%';` and query `WHERE Name LIKE :pattern`
questions.explain: Gluing user text into a query string lets the user change the query. That's **SOQL injection**. Use a bind variable, like `:pattern`, so the text is treated as data, never as SOQL.
wrong: Browser encoding is easy to skip, and it doesn't stop quotes reaching the query.
Sharing limits records, but injected filters still change the query.
Caching has nothing to do with input checks.
questions.source: Apex Developer Guide: SOQL Injection; Secure Coding Guide

questions.q: A new LWC works for admins, but sales users get an error saying they don't have access to the Apex class. The class is `with sharing`, and the users can read the objects. What should the developer do?
options: Give the users access to the Apex class through a permission set's Apex Class Access
Change the class to `without sharing`, so users without sharing access can still run it
Mark the method `@AuraEnabled(cacheable=true)`, which needs no Apex class permission
Make the class `global`, because only `global` classes can be called by every user
questions.explain: Signed-in users can call an `@AuraEnabled` method only with access to its Apex class. Grant it with Apex Class Access in a permission set or profile. Sharing and object access are separate checks.
wrong: Sharing mode doesn't grant access to the class itself.
Cacheable methods need class access too.
`global` is about namespaces, not user access.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Apex Class Access for @AuraEnabled methods; Salesforce Help: Set Apex Class Access

questions.q: A team reviews how its LWCs show text that users typed. Which two statements are true? (Choose 2)
options: Text bound with `{comment}` in a template is escaped, so markup in it shows as plain text
Setting `element.innerHTML = this.comment` in `renderedCallback()` is safe under Lightning Web Security
`lwc:dom="manual"` cleans anything that the component adds to that element by hand
Binding `{comment}` to an `href` is always safe, because attribute values are encoded
`lightning-formatted-rich-text` shows allowed formatting and strips unsafe tags and scripts
questions.explain: LWC templates escape bound text, so `{comment}` can't inject markup. For rich text, `lightning-formatted-rich-text` keeps safe formatting and removes the rest. Raw `innerHTML` skips these protections.
wrong: LWS isolates namespaces, but raw `innerHTML` with user text is still an XSS risk.
`lwc:dom="manual"` only lets you add DOM; it cleans nothing.
A value like `javascript:` in an `href` can still run code.
questions.source: LWC Developer Guide: Security with Lightning Web Security; lightning-formatted-rich-text

questions.q: After saving, a Visualforce controller sends users to the URL in the `retURL` page parameter. A review flags an open redirect. What is the best fix?
options: Wrap the value in `String.escapeSingleQuotes()` before building the `PageReference` object
Allow only relative paths that start with one `/`, and use a fixed page otherwise
Encode the value with `EncodingUtil.urlEncode()`, so that outside links can't be opened
Use `setRedirect(false)`, which keeps the browser inside Salesforce for any URL value
questions.explain: An open redirect lets a link send users from your page to an attacker's site. Check the value before you use it. Accept only paths inside your org, like ones starting with one `/`, else use a safe default.
wrong: That stops SOQL injection, not redirects.
Encoding the value doesn't stop a redirect to an outside site.
The redirect flag doesn't check where the URL points.
questions.source: Secure Coding Guide: Open Redirect
